paragraphs.zh: 复盘卡可以只留三行：原本的直接感谢、增加玩心后的版本、两版都保留的具体谢意。只改变比喻，别同时添加请求或扩大承诺，才容易说明自己比较了什么。若更喜欢直接版，也写下这一发现。这个虚构比较不补入过去四周的频率答案，也不把对方是否发笑当作效果分。
paragraphs.en: Keep a three-line review card: the direct thank-you, the version with play and the specific thanks both retain. Change only the image rather than adding a request or expanding a commitment, so you can explain what you compared. Record a preference for the direct version too. This fictional comparison does not enter your four-week frequency answers or turn another person’s laughter into an outcome score.

paragraphs.zh: 可以和同伴讨论：“同样感谢搬书，哪一处文字让语气变轻松？如果删掉，谢意还在不在？”先只谈句子，各自可以偏好不同版本，也可只看或不答。分享公开指南即可，不需要把均分、真实聊天或对方的反应拿出来证明自己温暖。
paragraphs.en: Ask together: “For the same thanks for moving books, which words make the tone playful, and does the thanks remain without them?” Discuss the sentence, allowing different preferences, observation or no answer. Share the public guide without using means, real chats or someone’s reaction as proof of warmth.

paragraphs.zh: 复盘卡可以并排放同一标题的两个虚构版本，标出唯一改变的词或颜色，再写“我想让这一处可见，其他部分保持原样”。把呈现内容和展示范围分开：喜欢一个亮点，不等于愿意公开整本。选原版、局部版或暂不展示都可以；这次想象不补入四周频率，也不统计赞美或曝光。
paragraphs.en: Place two invented versions of one title side by side, mark the only changed word or colour and note that this detail is visible while the rest stays as it was. Separate presentation from its audience: liking a highlight does not mean publishing the notebook. Keep either version or show neither. This imagined comparison does not enter the four-week frequencies or count compliments or exposure.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“只让标题有一点亮色，怎样说明想展示哪一处，而不用接受对整本作品或外貌的评价？”各给一种描述，再问是否准确表达了自己愿意展示的范围。可改变主意、只看或不答，不用照片、穿搭或个人均分作比较。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “With colour on the title alone, how would you describe what you want visible without inviting judgments on the notebook or your appearance?” Offer a description each and check its intended scope. Change your mind, observe or decline without comparing photographs, outfits or personal means.

paragraphs.zh: 复盘卡分成“直接描述”“意象描述”“我希望保留的细节”三栏。对同一虚构光线，只换一个词或一个意象，核它是否仍贴近原来想描述的画面；觉得意象添得太多时可以退回直接版。记录哪处更合适，而不追求更深刻。这张卡是新比较，不是过去四周已经发生的经历。
paragraphs.en: Use three columns: direct description, image-based description and the detail you want to retain. For the same invented light, change one word or image and check whether it still fits the intended scene. Return to the direct version if the image adds too much. Record fit rather than seeking greater depth. This card is a new comparison, not an experience that already occurred in the past four weeks.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“你从这两句看见的光线分别是什么？哪处是句子提供的，哪处是你自己的联想？”两人可以读出不同画面，回到文字核对即可，不必猜作者私人经历。可分享公开指南、只看或不答；不用审美、敏感程度或作品分数给人排名。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “What light do you imagine from each line, and which parts come from the words or your own associations?” Different pictures can be compared with the text without guessing the writer’s private history. Share the public guide, observe or decline without ranking taste, sensitivity or artwork.

paragraphs.zh: 复盘卡把一句安排划成“这次想保留”“仍可商量”“新条件出现后怎样改”三部分。例如保留一小排书的位置，其他布置待商量；若通道被占用，再说明需要换位置。检查句子是否把暂定偏好写成替双方作永久决定。修改可让条件更清楚，不代表均分应更高，也不把想象场面算进过去四周。
paragraphs.en: Divide a review card into what you want to retain this time, what remains open and how a new condition would change the plan. Retain a short row of books while discussing other details; if it obstructs a passage, state why its place should change. Check whether a provisional preference became a permanent decision for both people. Revision can clarify conditions without raising a mean or adding an imagined event to the four-week record.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“这句话已经决定哪一小段，还有哪一处需要我回应？如果条件变了，哪里可以改？”先复述对方的意思，再让对方纠正；理解清楚不要求最后同意。可只讨论虚构阅读角、只看或不答，不把配合、坚持或改口当成领导力和女性程度。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “Which part does this sentence settle, where can I respond and what could change with a new condition?” Restate the other person’s meaning and let them correct it; understanding requires no final agreement. Use the fictional reading corner, observe or decline without treating compliance, persistence or revision as leadership or femininity.
